prs.title: fix: terminate active StreamableHTTP sessions during shutdown
prs.author: weiguangli-io
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Active StreamableHTTP SSE connections aren't terminated cleanly when a session ends or the manager shuts down: terminate() doesn't close outstanding entries in self._sse_stream_writers, and task cancellation during shutdown causes EventSourceResponse coroutines to be killed mid-stream (ASGI incomplete-response warnings) instead of completing gracefully. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Active StreamableHTTP SSE connections aren't terminated cleanly when a session ends or the manager shuts down: terminate() doesn't close outstanding entries in self._sse_stream_writers, and task cancellation during shutdown causes EventSourceResponse coroutines to be killed mid-stream (ASGI incomplete-response warnings) instead of completing gracefully. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs build on the same self._sse_stream_writers mechanism for closing SSE connections from terminate(). #2253 implements both required halves: terminate() iterates self._sse_stream_writers, closes each writer, and clears the dict, and streamable_http_manager.py's lifespan is changed to call session termination before cancelling the task group on shutdown, which is what actually prevents the ASGI incomplete-response warnings. #3218 only adds the GET-stream registration (`self._sse_stream_writers[GET_STREAM_KEY] = sse_stream_writer` in _handle_get_request) so terminate() has something to close for that path, but its diff doesn't include the manager-shutdown ordering change, making it a partial fix that depends on #2253's terminate()-side logic already existing.

prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json() in func_metadata.py JSON-decodes string field values whenever the field's annotation is anything other than bare `str`. For a field typed as a Union that includes `str` (most commonly `Optional[str]` / `str | None`), a valid string value that happens to parse as JSON (e.g. a stringified payload) gets silently corrupted into a dict/list instead of being kept as a plain string. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json() in func_metadata.py JSON-decodes string field values whenever the field's annotation is anything other than bare `str`. For a field typed as a Union that includes `str` (most commonly `Optional[str]` / `str | None`), a valid string value that happens to parse as JSON (e.g. a stringified payload) gets silently corrupted into a dict/list instead of being kept as a plain string. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs gate pre_parse_json on the field's Union members instead of only the top-level type. #3056 adds _unwrap_annotated() and applies it before checking union members, so _is_optional_str correctly recognizes the common `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` pattern used for described optional parameters. #2032's _should_pre_parse_json instead checks each union arg for membership against a fixed frozenset {str, int, float, bool, NoneType} without unwrapping Annotated, so an Annotated-wrapped str member is not recognized as 'simple' and the original corruption still occurs for that common case. #2032 also disables pre-parsing for scalar unions that don't contain str at all (e.g. int | float) - a broader behavior change not required to fix the reported bug and with its own regression risk for numeric-string coercion.

clusters.pick_reason: Implements __reduce__ generically on the base MCPError class via `MCPError.__new__(error_type)` + `Exception.__init__(restored, *args)`, plus restores `self.__dict__` as pickle state — this covers every current and future MCPError subclass without per-class special-casing. Test coverage in this PR is extended beyond UrlElicitationRequiredError to also exercise NoBackChannelError, demonstrating the fix generalizes. #2555's __reduce__ is defined only on UrlElicitationRequiredError, so any other MCPError subclass with a non-matching constructor (e.g. NoBackChannelError) remains broken. #2478's `_restore_mcp_error` reconstructs via the classmethods `from_error_data`/`from_error` against the wire-format ErrorData rather than restoring `__dict__` state, so any instance attributes not represented in ErrorData are silently dropped on unpickle, and it still special-cases UrlElicitationRequiredError explicitly rather than deriving reconstruction purely from stored state.

clusters.pick_reason: #3252 and #2858 both narrow the critical section by moving the request `yield` outside the `async with self.context.lock` block, but continue to use a single `anyio.Lock`, which anyio requires to be released by the same task that acquired it — a hazard neither PR's diff addresses. #3243 replaces `context.lock` with `anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1)` plus a second `flow_lock` specifically because, per its own comment, httpx can resume or close the auth-flow generator from a different task than the one that yielded it, which would break a plain `anyio.Lock`; it also separates single-flight refresh/authorization serialization (`flow_lock`) from per-request locking (`lock`), a finer-grained fix than the other two.

clusters.pick_reason: Both add a check to reject a request id that's already in flight, but #3221 also introduces a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (prefixing int vs str ids with `i:`/`s:`) that #3063 lacks. clusters.pick_reason: Implements __reduce__ generically on the base MCPError class via `MCPError.__new__(error_type)` + `Exception.__init__(restored, *args)`, plus restores `self.__dict__` as pickle state — this covers every current and future MCPError subclass without per-class special-casing. Test coverage in this PR is extended beyond UrlElicitationRequiredError to also exercise NoBackChannelError, demonstrating the fix generalizes. #2555's __reduce__ is defined only on UrlElicitationRequiredError, so any other MCPError subclass with a non-matching constructor (e.g. NoBackChannelError) remains broken. #2478's `_restore_mcp_error` reconstructs via the classmethods `from_error_data`/`from_error` against the wire-format ErrorData rather than restoring `__dict__` state, so any instance attributes not represented in ErrorData are silently dropped on unpickle, and it still special-cases UrlElicitationRequiredError explicitly rather than deriving reconstruction purely from stored state.

clusters.pick_reason: #3252 and #2858 both narrow the critical section by moving the request `yield` outside the `async with self.context.lock` block, but continue to use a single `anyio.Lock`, which anyio requires to be released by the same task that acquired it — a hazard neither PR's diff addresses. #3243 replaces `context.lock` with `anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1)` plus a second `flow_lock` specifically because, per its own comment, httpx can resume or close the auth-flow generator from a different task than the one that yielded it, which would break a plain `anyio.Lock`; it also separates single-flight refresh/authorization serialization (`flow_lock`) from per-request locking (`lock`), a finer-grained fix than the other two.

clusters.pick_reason: Both add a check to reject a request id that's already in flight, but #3221 also introduces a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (prefixing int vs str ids with `i:`/`s:`) that #3063 lacks.
